hostCode.behaviour: The time axis is four canvas units per step of the diagram's unit from 1900-01, a month being `year × 12 + (month − 1)` written back as `YYYY-MM`; an unknown unit draws in months; rows are 56 units apart, a snap rounding halves away from zero.
A date is shown in the precision of the diagram's unit: `Jun 1795` in months, the year alone in coarser units.

A trend draws its first `phases` phases; each inner boundary is its dragged month when one is stored, otherwise spread evenly between its nearest dragged neighbours or the trend's ends, and a dragged boundary at or beyond the last visible phase is kept but not drawn.
A move shifts every dragged boundary by the months the trend moved; a span change scales each from the start by the new span over the old.
A boundary set is clamped so every visible phase stays at least a month long, against its nearest neighbours.
A span too short for its phase count is refused with "A trend showing N phases must be at least N months long, one per phase.".
A trend and a note are drawn from their top-left corner, a trigger from its centre; a trend is as wide as it lasts and a note as wide and tall as it keeps.
A move snaps a trend's or a note's left edge to the nearest step and its top to the nearest row, a trigger's centre to the nearest step and row; a trend keeps its length.

A drag of a trend's edge writes its start or its stop, its dragged boundaries scaled; a drag of a note's edge writes its size, and its month and row when the left or top border moved; any other edge is refused with "Only a trend's start and stop, and a note's borders, can be dragged.".
A point on the canvas is read by an addition as the month index and the row under it, fractional, in the diagram's unit.

A finished connect gesture draws an influence from the source's last visible phase, bottom, halfway, to the target's Peak, top, halfway; one from a trigger states no from end; into a trigger, onto itself or a second time in one direction it is refused.
A name is written trimmed and an empty one refused; a note's text is written with LF line breaks and no trailing ones.

A date typed in the grid sets the span with the dragged boundaries scaled; one boundary is clamped with the others, and only one between two visible phases may move; a phase count the span is too short for is refused.
Tags are written each once, in the order first written.

Arrange diagram packs trends, triggers and notes onto as few rows as their drawn extents allow, influenced trends on rows close together and a note over as many rows as it is tall; only `row` is written, in one step.

The Compact viewpoint shortens every trend to 24 canvas units per visible phase and packs it left in its row, causes before effects, 4 units apart; nothing of it is saved, and a drop on it means the true-time point the packing's inverse gives.

The ruler under the canvas labels the coarsest level whose labels stand 64 pixels apart: a month and a quarter as `MMM uuuu`, a year, a decade, a century and a millennium as `uuuu`, never finer than one step of the unit.
An element is named by the id the binding read into `storedId`; a date that is missing or does not read is none, a row or phase count that does not read is its fallback.
